paper: Echoes as Anchors: Probabilistic Costs and Attention Refocusing in LLM Reasoning

concepts.definition: Multi-step problem solving by large language models, including the trajectory by which a model keeps track of the original problem while generating intermediate reasoning steps.
Large language models optimized or prompted for multi-step reasoning.
The behavior where a model repeats or rephrases the original user question inside its reasoning trajectory.
A probabilistic measure used to quantify the likelihood effect of prompt echoes and connect early prompt repetition with reasoning performance.
A mechanism where prompt echoes shift model attention back toward important problem or answer-prefix tokens during reasoning.
A training-free inference-time strategy that reintroduces the original question or a reminder during generation to re-ground reasoning.
A supervised fine-tuning data strategy that encourages an echo-then-reason pattern.
A classifier or diagnostic tool used to detect patterns inside model reasoning traces, such as prompt repetition.
A failure mode where a model loses track of the original problem during a long reasoning trace.

Explaining model behavior through internal evidence: layer-wise attention analysis, probes, likelihood decomposition, and causal interventions. In this paper the analysis runs on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B over GSM8K; the answer-to-prefix attention gap is present at every layer group and peaks in mid-to-late layers (layers 7-18 Cohen's d = 0.832, against 0.820 early and 0.828 late). No neuron- or circuit-level claim is made.

Where reasoning tokens attend during multi-step generation. On DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B and GSM8K, correct traces attend more to the echoed answer prefix at every layer group (layers 7-18: 14.45% vs 11.58%), while in the token-wise test wrong traces attend significantly more to the raw question at 22 of 32 positions. The finding is a shift of attention between two targets rather than a one-sided effect.

Testing whether trace tokens do computational work by editing a trace and resuming generation under matched conditions. Reinserting an echo into previously failed GSM8K traces lifts exact match by +10.4 points (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B) and +7.9 points (Qwen3-8B), with a null result on the non-reasoning Qwen3-8B-Base. The inserted text is a fixed template phrase, so the result shows that mid-trace re-grounding is causally effective rather than that the spontaneous echo is.

Inference-time computation allocation in large reasoning models. EOP is framed as a front-loaded, compute-shaping mechanism. Echoic Prompting scored higher than thinking-token test-time scaling (TTTS) on AIME24 and MATH-500 under matched budgets, on a single model under greedy decoding and reported without numeric tables or error bars.

Keeping a reasoning trace anchored to the original problem. The paper motivates its anchoring account with positional-bias findings ('lost in the middle') and frames the echo prefix (mean about 219 tokens) as a self-generated re-injection of the problem statement. This is motivation rather than result: all experiments are short math traces and no long-context setting is tested.
